solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lower skirt, being embraced by stunner

indicators.note: the skirt word sits held inside the stunner word, as in a hug

parts.note: a stunner, a very attractive person, is a dish in slang
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: Someone lowers a skirt while being hugged by an attractive partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something is to reduce or lessen it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Old and regularly unsteady

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of unsteady, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An elderly person is described as old and frequently wobbly on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are second-hand, so not new: old in that sense.

clue.text: Force from cable in power line

indicators.note: in places the cable word inside the pair of letters for power and line

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: Force is drawn from a cable running in a power line.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something forward is to drive or push it: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Choke or accelerator

definitions.meaning: to choke someone is to strangle them by the throat
the lever controlling the fuel flow and so the speed of an engine

explanation.surface: A car-repair question: is it the choke or the accelerator?
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both to strangle and the valve controlling engine fuel, two distinct senses.

clue.text: He's nuts!

parts.note: reads as calling a man mad, but means a dealer in hardware such as nuts and bolts

explanation.surface: An exclamation that some man is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' here is metal fasteners, not madness: the man who sells them keeps a hardware shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardware dealer sells nuts, bolts and tools, so he is literally a man of nuts.

clue.text: Chap, for example, with ace wine cellar

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A man with a top-notch wine cellar is given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or wine shop, a borrowed word.

clue.text: States tour may start here

parts.note: airs are tunes or manners; to air views is to state them, so airs are states as a verb
a trip is a journey or tour

explanation.surface: A tour of the United States might begin from this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like America, but it is the verb: to air something is to state it. The whole clue also defines a strip where a flight, and so a tour, can begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing strip is where planes take off, so a journey by air may begin there.

clue.text: Particle, real or theoretical, of nucleus initially

definitions.text: Particle, real or theoretical, of nucleus initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A physics description of a particle in the nucleus, whether actual or hypothetical.
explanation.definitionFit: A positively charged particle found in every atomic nucleus, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: School's an aid to cultivation

definitions.meaning: a famous English public school in north-west London
a farm implement dragged over ploughed land to break up the soil

explanation.surface: A claim that schooling helps cultivate the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a well-known English private school; the 's is 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the English public school and a spiked frame used to level ploughed ground.

clue.text: Try holding on to right chick

indicators.note: holding on to means the try word grips the letter for right inside it

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep hold of the right young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird and chick are both informal British slang for a young woman, as well as feathered creatures.

clue.text: Sounded thick

definitions.meaning: spoken or uttered, as a word said out
strong and noticeable, as a thick accent

explanation.surface: Someone's voice came out heavy and dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both articulated in speech and marked or strongly noticeable, as of an accent.

clue.text: Relieve detective before endless shift

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector in the British police

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the shift word is dropped

parts.note: a spell is a period of work or shift

explanation.surface: A detective is relieved of duty before an unending work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel fears is to drive them away, so to relieve someone of them.

clue.text: Perform 'Under Pressure', Queen favourite, on speed

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a pet is a favourite
rate is a speed

explanation.surface: A singer performs Queen's favourite song Under Pressure at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under Pressure' is a hit by the band Queen, but here Queen is ER, the late monarch's cipher. 'on' places PET above RATE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime is to carry it out, so perform in that sense.

clue.text: Voluntary one found in irregular platoon

indicators.note: found in places the letter for one inside the rearranged platoon
irregular says the letters of platoon are put out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A volunteer turns up in an irregular army platoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' is a soldierly word in the surface, describing the platoon, but it is the anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something voluntary is not compulsory: left to choice, an exact synonym.

clue.text: The woman admitting a road's more complicated

indicators.note: admitting means the woman word lets the other letters in between hers

parts.note: her refers to the woman
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A woman concedes that a road is trickier than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Harder means more difficult, the same comparative sense as more complicated.

clue.text: Lift to reveal bum!

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky prank: lifting clothes to show a bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a noun for the backside but is the adjective meaning faulty, turning TO REVEAL into new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift is the British word for the device Americans call by this name.

clue.text: The man behind the counter?

parts.note: reads as a shop assistant, but means the scientist who gave his name to a radiation-detecting counter

explanation.surface: A question about who serves in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Geiger invented the radiation counter that carries his name, so he stands behind it.

clue.text: Grass, left inside, grassed

indicators.note: inside places the word for left within the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An informer is told to leave the grass while grassing others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grassed' is British slang for informed on the police; 'Grass' first is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for informing, so someone grassed has reported others to the police.

clue.text: Foreigners like eating porky new starter

indicators.note: eating means the like word swallows the other letters

parts.note: as means like
porky, from rhyming slang porky pie, means a lie

indicators.note: starter takes the first letter of new

explanation.surface: Foreigners seem to tuck into a pork-based starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porky' is British rhyming slang: porky pie means a falsehood. The surface suggests pork on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are people from other countries, a legal term for foreign nationals.

clue.text: Interior of planet here, almost unearthly

indicators.note: interior of means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Inside this planet things almost seem not of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or otherworldly, so not of this earth.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt to get prize

indicators.note: in places the work and hard letters inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
op, short for opus, is a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Working hard in an attempt to win an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or award won, a synonym for prize.

clue.text: Gruff sailor's game on exercise

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
RU stands for rugby union, a game
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A gruff sailor plays a game during training.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrupt manner is curt and brusque, much like gruff.

clue.text: Supports not starting dessert

indicators.note: not starting removes the first letter of the supports word

parts.note: rafters are the beams supporting a roof

explanation.surface: Supporters skip the starter and head for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British informal for pudding or dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Afters is a British colloquial word for the sweet course after the main.

clue.text: Turn on team broadcast for match

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered about means the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Turn on the TV: the team's game is broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a contest or series of games, so a match in a broad sense.

clue.text: Shakespeare is flipping tedious

indicators.note: flipping turns the tedious word backwards

parts.note: drab means dull or tedious

explanation.surface: Someone moans that Shakespeare is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word, but here it means turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard, the Bard of Avon, is the standard nickname for Shakespeare.

clue.text: Pearl's ace in garden

indicators.note: in places the ace letter inside the garden word

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Pearl, a gardener, is said to be excellent in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a small round gem, and a bead is a small round ball for stringing.

clue.text: Wind up around hard part of city

indicators.note: around has the wind-up phrase surrounding the letter for hard

parts.note: to get to someone is to annoy or wind them up
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Coming to a tough part of town can wind you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' is British slang for irritate: GET TO someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a segregated or deprived quarter of a city.

clue.text: He barely takes part in match!

definitions.text: He barely takes part in match!

parts.words: He barely takes part in match!
parts.note: reads as a reluctant player, but barely means naked: someone who runs nude across the pitch

explanation.surface: A footballer hardly gets involved in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means scarcely in the surface, but nude in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch invader who runs naked takes part, after a fashion, while bare.
